intro: A feature join can accidentally read the future. An as-of join selects the latest event available at each prediction time and makes unmatched queries explicit.
task: Join the latest available feature event to each prediction query without reading future observations.
requirements: event_times is a finite numeric vector, event_values is a finite (N,D) matrix with N matching times and D>0, and query_times is a finite vector. Inputs may be unsorted; N and query count may be zero.
For each query choose the event with maximum time <= query time. For tied event times choose the last original event row.

Return dict indices as integer event-row indices or -1, matched as a boolean vector, and values as a (Q,D) matrix. Unmatched rows contain zeros; use matched to distinguish missing data from actual zero-valued features.

Numeric inputs must be real and finite with magnitude at most 1e30, except where a stricter bound is stated. Booleans are not numeric parameters. Leave all caller inputs unchanged and raise ValueError for invalid inputs.

hints.title: Stable sorting resolves equal timestamps
hints.body: The last row among equal event times should remain last after sorting.

hints.title: Search on the right boundary
hints.body: A right-sided insertion point includes events exactly at query time; subtract one to get the latest eligible event.

explanation: A causal as-of join prevents temporal leakage by requiring every selected feature event to occur no later than the prediction query. Stable ordering gives a deterministic policy for repeated timestamps.
Event time is only one availability model. Real systems may also need ingestion-time constraints; this lesson makes its single-clock assumption explicit.
